• This bill creates three new laws: a Québec Constitution, an Act respecting constitutional autonomy, and an Act respecting the Constitutional Council.
  • It also amends 20 other laws to align them with these major changes.
Part 1 Québec Constitution
  • States that Québec takes precedence over any rule that contradicts it.
  • Defines the Québec nation and its collective rights, including equality between women and men.
  • Includes human rights and freedoms and fundamental language rights.
  • Sets out the roles of the legislative, executive, and judicial powers.
  • Sets out the principles guiding Québec in its relations with the outside world.
Part 2 Act respecting constitutional autonomy
  • Provides for special sittings of the National Assembly on constitutional issues.
  • Bars certain bodies from using public funds to challenge laws that protect Québec.
  • Requires the government to prepare a 10-year strategy on Québec's autonomy.
  • Allows the minister responsible for relations with Canada to give directives to government departments.
  • Allows the government to adopt a directive to prevent the federal government from encroaching on Québec's powers.
  • Requires an owner to notify the minister before transferring land to a federal institution, in certain cases.
  • Sets out Québec's role in the appointment of senators and Supreme Court judges.
Part 3 Act respecting the Constitutional Council
  • Creates a council that gives opinions on the Québec Constitution or on federal actions, at the request of the government or the Assembly.
  • Sets out how its members are appointed and how long they serve.
  • Allows the National Assembly's Office to adopt ethics rules for these members.
Part 4 Constitution Act, 1867
  • Removes the old rules on the Québec Legislative Council, which no longer exists.
  • Replaces the word "legislature" with "Parliament of Québec."
  • Adds state secularism, the model for integration into the Québec nation, and the civil law tradition as fundamental characteristics of Québec.
Part 5 Civil Code of Québec
  • Specifies that the Civil Code must be applied in harmony with the new Québec Constitution.
Part 6 Executive Power Act
  • Allows the premier to appoint a person to the position of "Officer of Québec."
Part 7 Charter of human rights and freedoms
  • Specifies that rights and freedoms must be interpreted taking into account the collective rights of the Québec nation.
  • Provides that in case of conflict, equality between women and men takes precedence over freedom of religion.
Part 8 Code of Civil Procedure
  • Sets rules for requests to suspend the application of a law passed by the Parliament of Québec.
  • Bars a court from raising a question of constitutionality on its own or forcing the parties to do so.
Part 9 Vocabulary change in all laws
  • "lieutenant governor" becomes "Officer of Québec" and "Executive Council" becomes "Council of Ministers."
Part 10 Charter of the French Language, Act respecting the laicity of the State, Act respecting integration into the Québec nation

26993:
• The bill simplifies the operating rules of professional orders (such as doctors, nurses, pharmacists) and expands what certain health professionals can do.
  • It gives more powers to the Office des professions du Québec, which oversees professional orders, to approve regulations without going through the Québec Cabinet.
Part 1 Professional Code
  • Professional orders will be able to adopt certain regulations themselves, without the approval of the Office or the Québec Cabinet.
  • The Office, rather than the Québec Cabinet, will now approve the codes of ethics of professional orders.
  • The Office will also decide which diplomas qualify a person for a permit or a specialist title.
  • The Office will have to create a common rule for all orders on how to settle disputes over professionals' bills.
  • The Office will be able to create rules affecting several professional orders at once.
  • The Office will alone set the ethics rules for members of the boards of directors of orders, and will be able to investigate and impose sanctions.
  • The public register of an order's members (the roll) will have to contain more information.
  • The minimum number of signatures needed to request a special general meeting changes.
  • People who obtained a psychotherapist permit elsewhere in Canada will be able to practise in Québec under new rules.
Part 2 Act respecting nurses
  • Nurses will be able to initiate exams and tests themselves, not only within public health activities.
  • They will be able to prescribe exams, tests, medications, substances, products and dressings, under rules to be set.
  • The rule that reserved voting rights at general meetings to section delegates only is removed.
Part 3 Midwives Act
  • Midwives will be able to prescribe and administer contraception more broadly.
  • They will be able to screen for sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections more broadly.
  • They will be able to treat these infections in a person without symptoms if their test is positive.
Part 4 Optometry Act
  • Optometrists will have fewer restrictions on the medications they can prescribe or administer and the care they can provide.
  • Dietitians will see their scope of practice expanded and will no longer need a medical prescription to carry out their reserved activities.
  • The Interdisciplinary Advisory Council on the Practice of Psychotherapy will cease operations.
  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a special permit, like psychologists and doctors.
  • The Office will be able to allow people in training to carry out certain psychotherapist activities before obtaining their full permit.
Part 5 Act respecting agronomists
  • An act will no longer need to be done for payment to be considered the practice of the profession of agronomist.
Part 6 Pharmacy Act
  • The Québec Cabinet will be able to allow a pharmacist to prescribe or substitute one medication for another made by a company in which they have a financial interest, under specific conditions.
Part 7 Act respecting prescription drug insurance
  • A new rule will allow a drug manufacturer to pay certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a banner or chain of pharmacies.
Part 8 Regulation respecting drug manufacturers and wholesalers
  • Manufacturers will also be able to pay these benefits to drug wholesalers.
  • Several other professional acts (land surveyors, notaries, the Barreau, denturology, medical imaging technologists) and regulations receive related consistency adjustments.

27679:
• The bill creates a new right allowing a person who is worried to obtain information about an intimate partner who may pose a risk to their safety.
  • It establishes a comprehensive process involving the Sûreté du Québec and a designated body to handle these requests and disclose the information.
  • New act respecting the disclosure of information: a person at risk, or someone acting on their behalf with their consent, may request information about their intimate partner.
  • New act: a minor aged 14 or over may submit such a request on their own.
  • New act: the government may, by regulation, designate other persons or categories of persons who may submit a request.
  • New act: police officers and workers from support organizations may inform a person at risk about the request process if it could benefit them.
  • New act: a police officer may, in these cases, disclose the identity of the partner who is the subject of a possible request.
  • New act: the Sûreté du Québec conducts the searches and transmits the relevant information to a body designated by the minister responsible for the status of women.
  • New act: a designated person, subject to regulatory conditions, meets with the person at risk to verbally communicate the information or the absence of relevant information.
  • New act: this person may also direct the person at risk to specialized resources and provide additional information.
  • New act: restrictions govern the disclosure to the intimate partner of the existence of a request and personal information concerning them.
  • New act: rules limit the further communication and use of the information obtained.
  • New act: certain persons benefit from immunity for acts performed in the exercise of their duties related to this process.
  • New act: these persons cannot be compelled to testify before a court concerning this information.
  • New act: penal offences are provided for breaches of the rules on communication or use of information.
  • Act respecting the Québec correctional system: revises the rules on disclosing to victims information concerning incarcerated persons or those under the supervision of correctional services.
  • Act respecting the Ministère de la Sécurité publique: consequential adjustments related to the creation of the new information disclosure regime.
